programmes.d: TV actor Emmanuel Lewis admits he watches The Tonight Show "only once in a blue moon." Comedian David Steinberg claims that nudity can be really boring.
Comic actor John Ritter whines about doing commercials, being student body president at Hollywood High, and getting his star on The Walk-of-Fame.
Grammy magnet Olivia Newton-John sings 2 of her numerous chart-topping tunes and fills in Johnny on growing up down under in Australia.
Dallas heartthrob Patrick Duffy says he always dreamed of becoming a TV star but now he wants to change his nice guy image. Also reveals his love for off-road racing.
10-year-old TV star Ricky Schroder (Silver Spoons) chats about his Mexico vacation, spending his earnings and his 2 girlfriends! Also tells Johnny the questions he does not like to be asked.
12-year-old TV star Ricky Schroder (Silver Spoons) shows off his skill juggling plastic eggs. Then Johnny gives it a try, unaware that Ricky swapped the plastic ones for real eggs. What a mess!
15-year-old TV star Ricky Schroder tells Johnny that when he gets his license, he wants to buy a Corvette. Also chats about dating, getting good grades in school and learning to sing.
The genius behind WKRP's Venus Flytrap, actor Tim Reid describes his experience auditioning for The Tonight Show. Also details his dream about his dear grandma.
Stand Up comedian Tim Thomerson announces he's leaving comedy to act in grade B sci-fi movies. His most recent role was as a time-traveling future cop in Trancers.
Dallas star Patrick Duffy commemorates Johnny's recent wedding, to wife #3, with a hilarious gift: A set of towels With Velcro monograms for quick switches.
Supermodel Christie Brinkley is also a boxing photographer? She fills in Johnny about her ringside gigs. Also talks about posing for Sports Illustrated's swimsuit issue and life in Malibu.
Super model Christie Brinkley describes doing photo shoots all over the world, and going skydiving, but chickening out at the last minute.
Oscar nom'd Amy Irving describes her kissing scene, with Barbra Streisand, in Yentl. Also fills in Johnny on her recent trip to Europe and her life at home in Santa Fe, New Mexico.
Supermodel Christie Brinkley chats about the hard work posing for Sports Illustrated's swimsuit issue and her upcoming marriage to Billy Joel, second time at the alter for both.
Fellow talk show host Alan Thicke discusses his early days playing in a band on a cruise ship. Also riffs hilariously on doing a sex seminar with Dr. Ruth.
Another superstar panel, with Lynn Redgrave and Tom Hanks, who talks about learning to juggle.
Richard Pryor discusses his latest film, "Superman," and seeing Ronald Reagan. Then Ally Sheedy talks about the transition from NYC to LA.
Stars of two of the televisions biggest shows join Johnny--Ted Danson (Cheers) and Courtney Cox (Friends).
Jeff Daniels discusses the amazing experience of working with Jack Nicholson on the film "Terms of Endearment."
Woody Harrelson talks about his latest film project, but he might be upstaged by the appearance of animal wrangler Sunni Black, who brings parrots and vultures to the show.
Famed Shakespearean actor Kenneth Branagh was young when he visited Johnny and talks about the thrill of meeting Kirk Douglas
Comedian Robert Klein regales Johnny with stories about growing up in the Bronx and kosher foods. Also on this episode is Kevin Spacey.
Tony Randall always lights up "The Tonight Show" panel and for this episode he's joined by Lara Flynn Boyle, who discussed "Twin Peaks."
Find out why is Kevin Pollack dressed as Cupid when he joins the show?
Comedian David Steinberg talks about going to Theological school before his career as a comedian. And Kenneth Branagh also joins the fun.
Glenn Close discusses two movies that couldn't be more different--"Fatal Attractions" and "The Big Chill."
